core.title: Write every component URN marker with all six segments in canonical order
core.given: An in-scope file carries a component URN marker (new, edited, or pre-existing and unchanged)
core.when: the marker is written, edited, or checked
core.then: The marker reads exactly the profile's component URN shape: the component artifact-kind literal first, then exactly five non-empty segments in canonical order — wagon, feature, component name, execution side, architectural layer.
prefer: During GREEN, derive each segment from the plan artifact, the file name, the execution side, and the architectural responsibility.
During GREEN, fix only the malformed or missing segment; keep already-correct identity segments unchanged.
avoid: When fixing URN grammar (do not broaden): inventing placeholder segments.
When fixing URN grammar (do not broaden): renaming implementation artifacts solely to make a guessed URN fit.
When fixing URN grammar (do not broaden): altering plan ownership.
unless: No component URN marker: skipped here; owned by the marker-presence rule.
Segment CONTENT is validated by the wagon-feature, name, side and layer rules; this rule checks shape only.
core.why: Each segment is a join key against the plan root: wagon and feature locate the work item, name the component, side and layer its architectural place. A URN missing a segment resolves to nothing — as unbound as no marker, while LOOKING traceable in review.
evidence: Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.
Prove: the URN has the canonical six-segment shape — the stack's traceability check reports no finding for this rule.
verification: The check parses each marker per the profile's component URN shape and requires exactly six segments — the artifact-kind literal first, none empty; any other segment count (fewer or more), a first segment other than the artifact-kind literal, or an empty segment is a finding. Detectable by a plain text scan of the scanned roots; no diff or phase observer required.

Files with no component URN marker are skipped — that finding belongs to the marker-presence rule; reporting both would double-count one fault. Pre-existing, unchanged markers are checked like new ones.
Shape only: segment values are validated by the wagon-feature, name, side and layer rules, not by this rule.
Severity 3. Disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding of this rule; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

Stack-neutral obligation with a per-stack detector: each realization enforces it with its own stack's traceability check, whose coverage is that stack's files; the obligation itself is not language-restricted.

fires: A file's component URN marker has fewer than six segments (one, two, three, four or five).
A file's component URN marker has seven or more segments (any count above six).
A component URN marker's first segment is anything other than the artifact-kind literal.
A component URN marker contains an empty segment.
A pre-existing, unchanged file carries a malformed component URN marker.
A coder writes or edits a component URN marker.
doesNotFire: A file has no component URN marker at all (owned by the marker-presence rule).
A marker has six well-formed segments but a segment's value is wrong (e.g. wrong side or layer) — owned by the wagon-feature, name, side and layer rules.

neutralityNotes: The six-segment canonical order and the segment meanings (wagon, feature, component name, side, layer) are method-level and stay in the core; the concrete spelling and separator (`component:{wagon}:{feature}:{Name}:{side}:{layer}`), the marker syntax (`URN:`), the plan root path (`plan/`) and the scan scope are profile data (urn.component, urn.binding.component, roots.plan, roots.scan). Detector, finding and sibling-rule ids (bun_green_traceability_detector, GREEN-URN-002, BUN-GREEN-URN-PATTERN-001, green-urn-marker, green-urn-wagon-feature, green-urn-name-matches, green-urn-side, green-urn-layer) remain Bun-only; the core names the check and the sibling rules generically. The concrete malformed-marker example (`component:w:f::side:layer`) is not repeated in the core — bun.json remains the worked reference example. Nothing else resisted neutralization.
